fact_check.claim: Collegetown is 0.1 to 0.5 miles from campus
Fall Creek 0.5 to 1 mile; downtown 0.5 to 1.5 miles; both a 20 to 30 minute uphill walk
fact_check.note: Matches. Cornell's Fall Creek and Commons text repeats the Downtown text word for word (the article flags this).

fact_check.claim: Collegetown walk up to 15 minutes, uphill from lower Collegetown
fact_check.note: Page says up to about 15 minutes; walk back from lower Collegetown is uphill.

fact_check.claim: Collegetown popularity 'increases rent, noise, and congestion'; mostly undergraduates
Cornell calls Collegetown a 'miniature city with shopping, restaurants and services'
fact_check.note: My fetch summary did not return this wording; writer should confirm the phrase against the page or paraphrase.

fact_check.claim: Fall Creek and downtown: lower rents by Cornell's account; many graduate students; frequent bus service
fact_check.note: Page says lower rents, city-neighborhood feel, many graduate students, 'Bus service is frequent in this area.'

fact_check.claim: Table: Fall Creek residents are 'Graduate students, families'
fact_check.note: Cornell says many graduate students; 'families' appears in no cited source.

fact_check.claim: Table: downtown residents are 'Grad and professional students, young professionals'
fact_check.note: Cornell says only 'many graduate students'. 'Professional students' and 'young professionals' are not in the cited sources.

fact_check.claim: Table: downtown bus 'the hub'; Collegetown bus 'Walkable, little need'
fact_check.note: Cornell does not mention buses for Collegetown and does not call downtown a hub. The paragraph under the table says all table rent/noise/walk data come from Cornell, but noise for Fall Creek and downtown does not.
Exact match; avg sizes 148, 433, 550 sq ft, so the 'very small unit sizes' caveat is right.

fact_check.claim: Fall Creek reviewers: quiet, far from Collegetown and fraternities, about 20 minute walk, mixed bus opinions; no median rent shown
fact_check.note: All confirmed. Page rating is 7.8/10 from 6 reviews, a thin base the article does not state.

fact_check.claim: Downtown: TCAT praised, flat and walkable, hill harder on foot, weekend Commons noise, festival crowds, limited food after 9 pm, safety concerns incl. break-in near an apartment building, 8.5/10 from 37 reviews
fact_check.note: Confirmed. Caveat: one reviewer calls the Commons only 'a little loud' and quiet soon after 1 am, another says quieter at night than Collegetown; table 'Loud near the Commons on weekends' overstates. Safety views are mixed.

fact_check.claim: New degree students ride TCAT free in first year; registered students free after 6 pm weekdays and all day weekends
OmniRide pass $200 a year, prorated monthly; PhD students and graduate assistants get one free
fact_check.note: Confirmed; page says the current rate shows at purchase.

fact_check.claim: 2022 Sun column: Collegetown listings over $1,000 a month per person; one-bedroom up to $2,625; students hunt in early fall, some sign more than a year ahead
fact_check.note: Confirmed (The Lux one-bedroom). Student-voice source, correctly dated 2022 and used as context, not as a current fact.

fact_check.claim: Many students begin looking between October and December
First- and second-year students should not sign a lease without an approved exemption; office can help review a lease
fact_check.note: Confirmed. The page appears partly outdated (2019-2020 deadline, mentions Colorado State), so the article should point to housing@cornell.edu / 607-255-5368 to confirm.

beats_top.query: collegetown vs fall creek vs downtown ithaca where to live
beats_top.why: The #1 result gives only character blurbs, a citywide median rent, no walk times or bus info; ours has the opening pick, Cornell distances, dated RentCafe figures, bus passes and a situation list. It is weakened by the table's unsourced resident and bus cells and by lacking any per-neighborhood rent.
changes: Remove unsourced cells so every table entry traces to a cited source
Add one concrete rent anchor for Fall Creek or downtown if an official or dated source exists, or state plainly that none exists in the table
Add a pointer to confirm exemption rules with Cornell Housing, since the marketplace page looks outdated

fixes: In the table, change Fall Creek 'Typical resident' from 'Graduate students, families' to 'Many graduate students (Cornell)'; source https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/housing/campus-housing/housing-search-process/ithaca-neighborhoods

In the table, change downtown 'Typical resident' from 'Grad and professional students, young professionals' to 'Many graduate students (Cornell)'; delete 'young professionals' unless you add a source.

In the table, change Collegetown Bus from 'Walkable, little need' to 'Cornell gives no bus info; walkable (up to 15 min)', and change downtown Bus from 'Frequent service, the hub' to 'Frequent service (Cornell); reviewers praise TCAT (VeryApt)'.

Change downtown Noise from 'Loud near the Commons on weekends' to 'Some weekend noise near the Commons, per reviewers (VeryApt, mixed)'; source https://www.veryapt.com/guides/neighborhood/366-ithaca-downtown-ithaca/

Rewrite the sentence under the table so it says distances, walk times and the Collegetown rent/noise remark come from Cornell, and Fall Creek and downtown noise come from VeryApt reviewers; link both.

Confirm the phrase 'miniature city with shopping, restaurants and services' against the Cornell neighborhoods page; if it is not word for word, paraphrase it without quotation marks or reword to match.

After the first-year/second-year lease sentence, add: 'The marketplace page looks partly out of date, so confirm your status with Cornell Housing (housing@cornell.edu, 607-255-5368) before signing'; source https://offcampus.housing.cornell.edu/
In the Fall Creek section, state that the VeryApt rating is 7.8/10 from 6 reviews, so readers see how thin the evidence is.
